module.title: Complex Nominalization: Transforming Verbs and Adjectives into Dense Academic Nouns
module.group: B2.3 - Strategic Debate & Bridge to C1
module.objective: Mengubah konstruksi klausa verbal menjadi frasa benda akademik yang padat dan berbobot ilmiah.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Greener Streets, Better Evidence
subModules.grammarFocus: Complex nominalization: changing verbs and adjectives into nouns and combining clauses into academic noun phrases
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Academic nouns for planning, evaluation, change, and evidence

content.summary: Read about a town that is considering changes to its transport system. You will follow the evidence behind the proposal and notice how academic writers turn actions and qualities into nouns. These noun forms can make information more compact, but it is still important to identify who acts and what happens.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Recognize nouns formed from verbs and adjectives, such as implementation, assessment, complexity, and reliability. Notice how a clause can become a noun phrase, for example, 'The council assessed the plan' becomes 'the council's assessment of the plan.'
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words for carrying out plans, evaluating evidence, describing change, and judging whether a proposal can work.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim each paragraph to identify its main point. Then scan for nominalized nouns and use nearby verbs, agents, and prepositions to work out what each noun refers to.

learningObjectives: Understand the main points in a B2 text about a town's transport proposal.
Locate details about the evidence, expected effects, and practical limits of the proposal.
Recognize common noun-forming suffixes, including -tion, -sion, -ment, -ance, -ence, -ity, -ness, and -cy.
Connect a compact noun phrase with the fuller clause it represents.
Use context to identify the action, quality, or person behind an academic noun.

contextWarmup.prompt: Your town is thinking about adding more cycle lanes. Which piece of information would be most useful before the council makes a decision?
options: A careful assessment of traffic, safety, and residents' needs
A list of the most popular bicycle colours
A prediction based only on one person's daily journey
contextWarmup.explanation: A careful assessment considers several relevant kinds of evidence. This makes it more useful for judging whether a proposal is suitable for the whole town.

rules: Many verbs form nouns with endings such as -tion, -sion, -ment, -ance, and -ence. For example, implement becomes implementation, assess becomes assessment, and resist becomes resistance. Check the spelling because the base word may change.
Many adjectives form nouns with endings such as -ity, -ness, and -cy. For example, complex becomes complexity, reliable becomes reliability, and possible becomes possibility.

A clause can be shortened into a noun phrase. 'The council assessed the proposal' can become 'the council's assessment of the proposal.' The noun often takes of to introduce its object, while by can name the agent.
Nominalization can make formal writing more compact, but it can also hide the person responsible for an action. Look for by-phrases, possessives, and surrounding sentences to identify the agent.

commonTrap.explanation: A nominalized noun does not work like a verb. Do not put a direct object immediately after it as if it were still a verb. A noun such as assessment usually connects to its object with of.
commonTrap.wrong: The assessment the new route took six months.
commonTrap.correct: The assessment of the new route took six months. Alternatively: The team assessed the new route over six months.

content.contractionsSubtitle: Formal reports often use full forms, while people discussing the same ideas may use contractions:

contractions.subject: It
contractions.exampleFull: It is difficult to assess the plan without local traffic data.
contractions.exampleContracted: It's difficult to assess the plan without local traffic data.

contractions.subject: They
contractions.exampleFull: They are reviewing the feasibility study this week.
contractions.exampleContracted: They're reviewing the feasibility study this week.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Nominalization
grammarFormulas.description: Compare a direct clause with a compact noun phrase. The noun phrase can be used as the subject of a new sentence.

complements.type: Object of the verb or noun
Prepositional phrase after a nominalized noun

items.exampleSentence: The implementation of the new bus timetable will begin in September.
The report includes an acknowledgement of the noise caused by construction.
The complexity of the transport network makes planning difficult.
An assessment of road safety will be completed before work begins.
The emergence of low-cost electric bikes has changed how some residents travel.
Temporary disruption is expected while the bridge is repaired.
The reliability of the evening bus service is important to hospital staff.
Residents reported a deterioration in air quality near the main road.
The establishment of a residents' group gave local people a way to share concerns.
The council requested a feasibility study before approving the bridge project.

paragraphs: For years, Riverton residents complained about slow buses and crowded roads near the town centre. The emergence of inexpensive electric bikes also changed travel habits, but not everyone felt safe cycling beside heavy traffic. In response, the council proposed a protected cycle route linking the railway station with three schools and the public library. Rather than approve the plan immediately, it asked a local university to assess its likely effects.

The assessment included traffic counts, interviews with residents, and a review of accident reports. Researchers found that the greatest complexity lay in the narrow streets around the market. A cycle lane there could reduce delays for cyclists, but it might also restrict deliveries to small shops. The report acknowledged this problem and recommended a short trial, with delivery times clearly marked. It also found that air quality had deteriorated beside two busy roads over the previous five years.

The council then considered the feasibility of the proposal. Engineers estimated that construction would take four months, during which temporary disruption was likely. The reliability of the route would depend on regular maintenance and clear signs, especially in winter. To address concerns, the council held public meetings and recorded residents' suggestions. The establishment of a neighbourhood transport group followed, giving shop owners, parents, and cyclists a place to discuss changes.

The implementation is planned in two stages. First, the council will build a short section near the schools and collect information on traffic, safety, and use. It will publish the results before deciding whether to extend the route to the library and station. This approach will not remove every disagreement, but it makes the decision easier to review. Instead of promising that the plan will solve all traffic problems, the council says its next step will depend on the evidence.

questions.question: Why did the council ask a university to assess the proposal?
options: It wanted information about the proposal's likely effects before approving it.
It wanted the university to build the cycle route.
It wanted to replace the local schools.
questions.answer: It wanted information about the proposal's likely effects before approving it.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says the council did not approve the plan immediately and asked a university to assess its likely effects.

questions.question: What did the researchers identify as the greatest complexity?
options: The narrow streets around the market
The distance between the library and the station
The lack of electric bikes in Riverton
questions.answer: The narrow streets around the market
questions.explanation: The second paragraph states that the greatest complexity lay in the narrow streets around the market.

questions.question: What possible problem could the cycle lane cause for small shops?
options: It could restrict deliveries.
It could close the public library.
It could make winter signs unnecessary.
questions.explanation: The report noted that a cycle lane near the market might restrict deliveries to small shops.

questions.question: What did the report recommend to deal with delivery concerns?
options: A short trial with clearly marked delivery times
A permanent road closure without a trial
Moving all the shops to the railway station
questions.answer: A short trial with clearly marked delivery times
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says the report recommended a short trial and clearly marked delivery times.

questions.question: What had happened to air quality beside two busy roads?
options: It had deteriorated over the previous five years.
It had improved because the route was already built.
It had not been measured.
questions.answer: It had deteriorated over the previous five years.
questions.explanation: The researchers found that air quality had deteriorated beside two busy roads over five years.

questions.question: How long did engineers expect construction to take?
options: Four months
Five years
One week
questions.explanation: The third paragraph reports the engineers' estimate of four months for construction.

questions.question: What would the route's reliability depend on?
options: Regular maintenance and clear signs
A larger market and more shops
The removal of all public meetings
questions.explanation: The passage directly says the route's reliability would depend on regular maintenance and clear signs.

questions.question: What was the result of establishing a neighbourhood transport group?
options: Different local people gained a place to discuss changes.
The council ended its assessment of the route.
The group immediately extended the route to the station.
questions.answer: Different local people gained a place to discuss changes.
questions.explanation: The group gave shop owners, parents, and cyclists a place to discuss changes.

questions.question: What will the council do before deciding whether to extend the route?
options: Build a short section and publish information about its results
Build the entire route without collecting information
Wait until all residents agree with every part of the plan
questions.answer: Build a short section and publish information about its results
questions.explanation: The final paragraph says the council will first build a short section, collect information, and publish the results.

questions.question: In the phrase 'the reliability of the route', what does the noun 'reliability' describe?
options: How consistently well the route is expected to work
Who first suggested the route
How much the route will cost to build
questions.answer: How consistently well the route is expected to work
questions.explanation: Reliability means the quality of working consistently well. The passage links it to maintenance and clear signs.

content.summary: This briefing prepares you to listen to two researchers discussing abstract revisions. You will track how casual conversational phrases transform into dense nominalized structures, while also identifying connected speech features like consonant linking, flap sounds, and vowel reduction.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of an editorial critique regarding research writing.
Identify specific suggestions for replacing verb clauses with noun phrases.
Notice sound reductions and linking patterns in rapid spoken academic guidance.

keyPhrases.meaning: perumusan kalimat akademik yang lebih ringkas dan padat
keyPhrases.note: Used by authors when editing out wordy verbal descriptions.
A classic nominalized frame replacing 'when we analyzed the data'.

keyPhrases.meaning: mengubah setiap kata kerja menjadi kata benda
keyPhrases.note: Refers to the potential mistake of overloading text with noun forms.
Emphasizes retaining readability alongside technical density.

connectedSpeech.slow: Let me take a quick look
connectedSpeech.note: The /t/ in 'let' assimilates into /m/, and 'take a' links smoothly into a single unit.
Final consonant /t/ links directly to the vowel in 'into', and an intrusive r sound often connects 'data' and 'analysis'.
The final /s/ sound in 'balance' connects across the word boundary to 'is'.
The stop consonant /d/ links right into the diphthong /aɪ/ without a pause.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Build Dense Academic Noun Phrases

content.summary: Nominalization changes verbs and adjectives into nouns. Academic writers use nominalized nouns to express complex ideas in fewer words and to focus on actions, results, or qualities rather than on the people who perform them. Use nominalization carefully: too many noun phrases can make writing difficult to read.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Form Nouns from Verbs
blueprintItems.example: The team developed a new method. → The development of a new method took several months.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Form Nouns from Adjectives
blueprintItems.example: The system is efficient. → The efficiency of the system reduced costs.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Turn a Clause into a Noun Phrase
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + verb + object → The + nominalized verb + of + object + by + agent
blueprintItems.example: Scientists discovered a new species. → The discovery of a new species by scientists attracted attention.

mechanicsRules.rule: Choose the correct noun form because suffixes do not follow one fixed pattern. Check the spelling and use a dictionary when necessary.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The develop of the plan took two years.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The development of the plan took two years.
mechanicsRules.why: The noun form of develop is development, not develop.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use of to connect a nominalized noun to its object. Use by to name the person or group responsible for an action when that information matters.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The discovery a new species by scientists was unexpected.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The discovery of a new species by scientists was unexpected.
mechanicsRules.why: The noun discovery is followed by of before the thing discovered.

mechanicsRules.rule: Keep a clear subject and verb in the main clause, even when the sentence begins with a long noun phrase.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The analysis of the results by the researchers.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The analysis of the results by the researchers revealed a clear pattern.
mechanicsRules.why: The original example is a noun phrase, not a complete sentence, because it has no main verb.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Report a Research Finding
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three or four sentences about a research finding. Use at least two nouns formed from verbs, such as development, resistance, or discovery. Include a complete main clause in each sentence.
guidedLabChallenges.example: The development of the new test took six months. Its accuracy improved after further testing. The researchers reported the improvement in a journal.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Explain a Change
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write a short paragraph explaining a change in a process or system. Use at least one adjective-based noun, such as complexity, awareness, or efficiency, and connect two ideas with although, because, or while.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Although the complexity of the system increased, its efficiency also improved. This change resulted from careful planning by the engineering team.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Explain the change in a short paragraph...

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence as a noun phrase followed by a complete main clause. Keep the agent.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The engineers improved the design, and this reduced production time.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change improved to improvement and use of the design and by the engineers.
targetAnswers: The improvement of the design by the engineers reduced production time.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Improved becomes improvement. The phrase of the design names what changed, while by the engineers identifies the agent.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Replace the adjective clause with an adjective-based noun phrase.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The procedure is complex, so it requires extra training.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change complex to complexity and make it the subject of the sentence.
targetAnswers: The complexity of the procedure means that it requires extra training.
The complexity of the procedure requires extra training.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Complexity is the noun form of complex. The rewritten sentence keeps the original idea and has a complete main clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the first clause into a noun phrase and keep the cause-and-result relationship.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The researchers discovered a weakness, so the team revised the plan.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the discovery of a weakness by the researchers as the subject.
targetAnswers: The discovery of a weakness by the researchers led the team to revise the plan.
The discovery of a weakness by the researchers caused the team to revise the plan.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Discovery is the noun form of discover. The phrase of a weakness names what was discovered, and by the researchers names the agent.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the ideas using although and the noun complexity.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The process is complex. It remains efficient.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with Although the complexity of the process.
targetAnswers: Although the complexity of the process is high, it remains efficient.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Although introduces a contrast. Complexity is the noun form of complex, and the sentence still includes a complete main clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the ideas using because and the noun development.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The company developed a safer material. The product became more reliable.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use because the company developed or because of the development of.
targetAnswers: The product became more reliable because the company developed a safer material.
The product became more reliable because of the development of a safer material by the company.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because can introduce a clause, while because of is followed by a noun phrase. The second answer nominalizes developed as development.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the spelling and punctuation in this sentence.
practicumQuestions.promptText: the resistence of the material to heat surprised the engineers
practicumQuestions.hint: Use resistance, capitalize the first word, and add a full stop.
targetAnswers: The resistance of the material to heat surprised the engineers.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The correct spelling is resistance. A complete sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the noun form and missing preposition.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The discover a new species by scientists was reported yesterday.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use discovery and place of before a new species.
targetAnswers: The discovery of a new species by scientists was reported yesterday.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Discovery is the noun form of discover. Use of to introduce what was discovered.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using an adjective-based noun phrase.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The system is efficient, and this saves energy.
targetAnswers: The efficiency of the system saves energy.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Efficiency is the noun form of efficient. It can act as the subject of the new sentence.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write one complete academic sentence using commitment as a nominalized noun.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Express the idea that the students committed themselves to the project and completed it.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the commitment of the students to the project as a noun phrase.
targetAnswers: The commitment of the students to the project led to its completion.
The students' commitment to the project resulted in its completion.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Commitment is the noun form of commit. The noun phrase can identify who made the commitment and what they committed themselves to.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write one sentence that nominalizes an action and connects it to a result with therefore or as a result.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Use resistance in a sentence about a material that prevents damage.
practicumQuestions.hint: Make resistance the subject, and include a complete main clause.
targetAnswers: The resistance of the material to heat prevented damage; therefore, the equipment remained safe.
The material showed resistance to heat. As a result, the equipment remained safe.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Resistance is the noun form of resist. Therefore and as a result connect a cause with its consequence, and each version contains complete clauses.

content.summary: Practise turning verbs and adjectives into nouns to express ideas concisely in formal speech. For example, “The team implemented the policy” can become “The implementation of the policy by the team.” Use nominalized phrases when they make your point clearer, and include a clear main verb in the full sentence.
content.audioGuidance: Say long academic nouns in steady syllables, with the main stress clearly marked. Pause briefly before a long noun phrase, then connect its words smoothly. Keep the sentence's main verb prominent so that dense wording remains easy to follow.

pillars.name: Syllable Stress
pillars.target: Emphasise the main stress in academic nouns
pillars.explanation: Many noun endings, such as -tion, -ment, and -ity, add syllables. Practise words such as implementation, assessment, and reliability without rushing their unstressed syllables.

pillars.name: Clear Nominalization
pillars.target: Turn actions and qualities into precise nouns
pillars.explanation: Change a clause such as “The system became more reliable” into “The system's increased reliability.” Keep the meaning and the relationship between ideas clear.

pillars.name: Natural Sentence Rhythm
pillars.target: Balance dense noun phrases with clear pauses
pillars.explanation: Group related words together, for example, “a comprehensive assessment of student performance.” Avoid placing so many nouns together that listeners lose track of the main point.

pillars.name: Controlled Intonation
pillars.target: Use falling intonation for completed points
pillars.explanation: Use a steady fall at the end of a complete statement. Use a rise when checking information or inviting a response in a discussion.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: The stress moves from the fourth syllable in implementation to the third syllable in implemented.
The main stress stays on the second syllable in both forms.
The main stress changes position: it falls on the fourth syllable in reliability and the second in reliable.
The main stress shifts from the fifth syllable in deterioration to the second syllable in deteriorate.

drills.targetText: The implementation of the new policy requires cooperation across departments.
drills.phonetic: /ði ˌɪmplɪmenˈteɪʃən əv ðə njuː ˈpɒləsi rɪˈkwaɪəz kəʊˌɒpəˈreɪʃən əˈkrɒs dɪˈpɑːtmənts/
drills.focus: Primary stress in implementation and cooperation
drills.hint: Keep the final syllable of implementation unstressed, and place the main stress on TA.

drills.targetText: A careful assessment of the proposal revealed its complexity.
drills.phonetic: /ə ˈkeəfəl əˈsesmənt əv ðə prəˈpəʊzəl rɪˈviːld ɪts kəmˈpleksəti/
drills.focus: Word stress and linking in a formal sentence
drills.hint: Give assessment a clear second-syllable stress, then connect “assessment of” smoothly.

drills.targetText: The reliability of the results depends on the quality of the data.
drills.phonetic: /ðə rɪˌlaɪəˈbɪləti əv ðə rɪˈzʌlts dɪˈpendz ɒn ðə ˈkwɒləti əv ðə ˈdeɪtə/
drills.focus: Syllable clarity in reliability and natural sentence rhythm
drills.hint: Slow down slightly on reliability, then make the main verb depends easy to hear.

drills.targetText: The emergence of digital services caused disruption in local businesses.
drills.phonetic: /ði ɪˈmɜːdʒəns əv ˈdɪdʒɪtəl ˈsɜːvɪsɪz kɔːzd dɪsˈrʌpʃən ɪn ˈləʊkəl ˈbɪznəsɪz/
drills.focus: Contrastive stress and clear noun endings
drills.hint: Keep disruption distinct from the words around it, and finish the sentence with a falling tone.

roleplay.context: You are taking part in a university project meeting about a proposed public transport policy. Discuss its feasibility, likely implementation, and possible disruption. Use nominalized phrases to present your points clearly.

turns.speaker: Project Adviser
turns.text: What is your assessment of the proposal's feasibility?
turns.translation: Bagaimana penilaian Anda terhadap kelayakan usulan ini?

turns.speaker: Student Researcher
turns.text: Our assessment suggests that the implementation is feasible, although the cost remains a concern.
turns.translation: Penilaian kami menunjukkan bahwa penerapannya layak, meskipun biayanya masih menjadi perhatian.

turns.speaker: Project Adviser
turns.text: How might the establishment of this service affect local businesses?
turns.translation: Bagaimana pembentukan layanan ini dapat memengaruhi usaha setempat?

turns.speaker: Student Researcher
turns.text: The initial disruption may be significant, but improved reliability could benefit businesses in the long term.
turns.translation: Gangguan awal mungkin cukup besar, tetapi peningkatan keandalan dapat menguntungkan usaha dalam jangka panjang.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds about a change you have experienced at school, work, or in your community. Use at least two nominalized forms.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a change, explain how it was introduced, and say what effect it had.
storyPoints: Describe the change and the reason for its implementation.
Explain how people responded to it, including any acknowledgement of problems.
Give your assessment of its impact and say whether the change should continue.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The implementation of the new timetable improved organisation, although the initial disruption caused some confusion.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ði ˌɪmplɪmenˈteɪʃən əv ðə njuː ˈtaɪmteɪbəl ɪmˈpruːvd ˌɔːɡənaɪˈzeɪʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Tell a clear sequence of events and use nominalization where it makes your description more concise.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds about a problem that became more complicated over time. Use at least two nominalized forms.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell a short story about a problem, its development, and a possible response.
storyPoints: Introduce the original problem and explain how its complexity increased.
Describe an important development or change that affected the situation.
Recommend a response and explain how its feasibility could be assessed.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The increasing complexity of the issue made a careful assessment of possible solutions necessary.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ði ɪnˈkriːsɪŋ kəmˈpleksəti əv ði ˈɪʃuː meɪd ə ˈkeəfəl əˈsesmənt əv ˈpɒsəbəl səˈluːʃənz ˈnesəsəri/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use time markers to organise your story, and make the relationship between each nominalized phrase and the main verb clear.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live call with a research coordinator. Explain how a study will be carried out and respond to questions using nominalized forms.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: You are discussing the implementation of a student feedback study.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A research coordinator is calling to confirm the study plan. You must describe the assessment process, identify a possible difficulty, and suggest a practical response.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the student researcher. The AI plays the research coordinator.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The implementation of the survey requires careful planning and an assessment of response rates.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ði ˌɪmplɪmenˈteɪʃən əv ðə ˈsɜːveɪ rɪˈkwaɪəz ˈkeəfəl ˈplænɪŋ ənd ən əˈsesmənt əv rɪˈspɒns reɪts/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Answer the coordinator directly, use formal noun phrases, and keep your spoken responses clear.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live call with a project adviser. Discuss whether a proposed transport service can be introduced.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The adviser asks about the feasibility and possible disruption of a new bus service.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A local council is considering a new bus service. Discuss the feasibility of implementation, possible disruption during construction, and the information needed before a decision.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a community project assistant. The AI plays the project adviser.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: A feasibility study should include an assessment of cost and possible disruption.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ə ˌfiːzəˈbɪləti ˈstʌdi ʃəd ɪnˈkluːd ən əˈsesmənt əv kɒst ənd ˈpɒsəbəl dɪsˈrʌpʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Give reasons for your recommendation and use nominalizations to group related details.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live call with an environmental officer. Discuss changes to a coastal area and recommend a response.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The officer asks you to explain the deterioration of the coastline and its effects.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A council is reviewing reports of coastal deterioration. Discuss its possible causes, effects on local communities, and the establishment of a monitoring programme.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a community research assistant. The AI plays the environmental officer.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The deterioration of the coastline highlights the need for the establishment of regular monitoring.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə dɪˌtɪəriəˈreɪʃən əv ðə ˈkəʊstlaɪn ˈhaɪlaɪts ðə niːd fə ði ɪˈstæblɪʃmənt əv ˈreɡjələ ˈmɒnɪtərɪŋ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describe the issue and its consequences, then make a specific recommendation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live call with a business adviser. Explain how a new technology has affected a local business.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The adviser wants to know how digital change has affected business operations and what should happen next.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A local shop has introduced online ordering. Discuss the emergence of this service, the disruption during the change, and the reliability of the new system.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the shop's operations assistant. The AI plays the business adviser.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The emergence of online ordering brought disruption, but improvements in system reliability have helped the business.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ði ɪˈmɜːdʒəns əv ˈɒnlaɪn ˈɔːdərɪŋ brɔːt dɪsˈrʌpʃən bət ɪmˈpruːvmənts ɪn ˈsɪstəm rɪˌlaɪəˈbɪləti həv helpt ðə ˈbɪznəs/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Balance the difficulties and benefits in your answer, and use a clear contrast between them.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say each clause again using the noun in brackets. Then combine your ideas into one clear sentence.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Change “The team implemented the policy” using implementation. Change “The system became reliable” using reliability. Change “The issue became complex” using complexity.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The implementation of the policy improved reliability, despite the complexity of the issue.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ði ˌɪmplɪmenˈteɪʃən əv ðə ˈpɒləsi ɪmˈpruːvd rɪˌlaɪəˈbɪləti dɪˈspaɪt ðə kəmˈpleksəti əv ði ˈɪʃuː/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use each noun accurately and include an appropriate article or preposition where needed.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform each clause into a noun phrase, then say one full sentence containing the phrase. Keep the original meaning.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Transform “The organisation established a programme” using establishment. Transform “Researchers assessed the plan” using assessment. Transform “The new service disrupted trade” using disruption.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The establishment of the programme followed an assessment of the plan, despite concerns about disruption.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ði ɪˈstæblɪʃmənt əv ðə ˈprəʊɡræm ˈfɒləʊd ən əˈsesmənt əv ðə plæn dɪˈspaɪt kənˈsɜːnz əˈbaʊt dɪsˈrʌpʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use the correct noun form and connect it to the rest of the sentence with an appropriate preposition.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Repeat each word, emphasising the stressed syllable. Then say the model sentence at a steady pace.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Practise implementation, acknowledgement, assessment, and feasibility. Keep the unstressed syllables light and distinct.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: An acknowledgement of the issue led to an assessment of the proposal's feasibility.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ən əkˈnɒlɪdʒmənt əv ði ˈɪʃuː led tə ən əˈsesmənt əv ðə prəˈpəʊzəlz ˌfiːzəˈbɪləti/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Place the main stress on the correct syllable: the second in acknowledgement, the second in assessment, and the third in feasibility.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the first sentence as a completed statement with falling intonation. Say the second as a genuine checking question with rising intonation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Practise a fall at the end of a conclusion and a rise when checking whether the listener agrees.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The reliability of the findings has improved. Do you agree?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə rɪˌlaɪəˈbɪləti əv ðə ˈfaɪndɪŋz həz ɪmˈpruːvd. də juː əˈɡriː/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use falling intonation for the completed statement and a rising tone for the checking question.
